topic: the hidden design rules behind national flag colors and shapes
title: Why So Many Flags Share the Same 3 Colors
description: AI-narrated commentary exploring the surprising history and hidden 'rulebook' behind national flag design -- why so many flags share the same colors, why the US flag has been redesigned dozens of times, and why one country's flag isn't even a rectangle.

hook_candidates.text: Why do so many national flags use almost the exact same three colors?
One country's flag has been redesigned twenty-seven times, and it's not the one you're thinking of.
You probably think flag colors are just a design choice. They're actually a coded rulebook.
In 1912, a US president signed one order that finally fixed a century of flag chaos.

beats.text: Why do almost half the world's flags use the exact same three colors?
Turns out red, white and blue isn't a coincidence, it's a shared code. Red usually means sacrifice, white means purity, blue means vigilance or justice.
Even the shapes aren't random. For over a century, the American flag alone was redesigned twenty-seven times as states joined.
There wasn't even a fixed star pattern until nineteen twelve, when a president finally standardized the rows we recognize today.
Some countries skip the rulebook completely. Nepal's flag isn't even a rectangle, it's the only one shaped like that in the world.
So next time you see a flag, you're looking at a coded design document. What's a flag detail you never noticed? Tell me below.
